warnings.title: Spurious UnusedStrategyHole warning for a hole referenced ONLY in a shared-len position
warnings.description: The unused-hole tracking set `referenced_holes` is populated ONLY by `collect_hole_refs_in_args`, which walks annotation args (@workgroup etc.). M3.22 introduced a NEW hole reference site — `shared[T, ?name]` length — but that site is NOT added to `referenced_holes`. Consequence: a @strategy hole used exclusively in a shared-len position (e.g. AT-2984·A's own fixture `@workgroup(64,1,1) @strategy { WG: ?[32,64] } ... shared t: shared[i32, ?WG]`) is spuriously reported `HirWarning::UnusedStrategyHole { name: "WG" }` on the RAW lower path (discovery / run_optimize / fail-closed compile), even though WG IS genuinely used.
warnings.evidence: Reproduced directly: `axc compile fixture.axc` (no assignment) emits `warning: UnusedStrategyHole { name: "WG" }` immediately before the (correct) `UnresolvedStrategyHole` codegen error. two_pass_reduce and the AT-2984·B fixture do NOT trip it only because WG is ALSO used in `@workgroup(?WG)` there (collected from the annotation). The textual --strategy-value path never trips it because substitution removes the hole pre-parse.
warnings.impact: Cosmetic / diagnostic-accuracy only. NON-BLOCKING: the hole is still discovered and enumerated (AT-2984·A completes, winner .spv correctly sized to WG, both AT-2984·B variants enumerate), codegen and correctness are unaffected. Not covered by any AT. Route to Architect as a one-line follow-up (add shared-decl len_hole names to `referenced_holes`) or a defer-list row.

warnings.title: AT-2984·A's OpTypeArray-length assertion is a loose OpConstant scan, not an OpTypeArray-length-operand check
warnings.description: AT-2984·A verifies the winner .spv's shared length via `asm_has_opconstant_value(asm, winning_wg)`, which returns true if ANY disassembled line contains `OpConstant` and ends with the winning value's token. It does NOT resolve the OpTypeArray's length-operand id back to its OpConstant. If a future codegen change introduced an unrelated `OpConstant <winning_wg>` (e.g. a loop bound coincidentally equal to WG) the assertion could pass even if the array were mis-sized. Also, the .spv and the sidecar are both written from the SAME in-memory winner_assignments, so this is winner-internal-consistency, not a recompile-and-cmp cross-validation.
warnings.evidence: Independently disassembled the substituted artifacts by parsing OpTypeArray(op=28) -> length-operand -> OpConstant(op=43): WG=32 yields OpTypeArray length constant 32, WG=64 yields 64 (the STRONG check the test approximates). Byte-cmp of the two variants differs at the length constant only. So the fix is correct; the test's phrasing of the check is just weaker than its own docstring claims ("OpTypeArray shared length equal to the winning WG").
warnings.impact: Test-robustness nit. The underlying behavior is correct (verified by exact operand-resolving disasm + AT-2975 byte-identity + AT-2984·B real dispatch). Not blocking.

warnings.title: Spec §1.3's F2-strip justification for the codegen backstop is slightly imprecise (defense is actually stronger)
warnings.description: §1.3 motivates `CodegenError::UnresolvedSharedLenHole` by 'F2 strips the @strategy block, so a shared-len hole would slip past the strategy-hole backstop'. In reality, on ANY textual F2-strip path the NEW lower.rs check (288-306) fires `HirError::UndefinedStrategyHole` at the driver's HIR-error gate BEFORE codegen (verified: MCP compile_variant with empty map fails HIR-level, never reaches emit). The codegen backstop's genuinely-sole-guard role is the ENUMERATOR path (`resolve_single_variant` -> `emit_module`), where @strategy is present at lower time (so no UndefinedStrategyHole) but the variant assignment may omit the hole name (AT-2983 negative). Both paths fail closed; the guarantee holds. This is a doc-precision note, not a code defect — QA flagged the same nuance.
warnings.impact: None. Fail-closed is proven on every path exercised.

summary: APPROVE. M3.22 is a clean, validation-only cleanup: the shared[T,?name] parser fix carries the hole as additive metadata (SharedTy.len stays u32), resolves it at both the textual-substitution and enumerator points, and fails closed via a single codegen backstop; validate() and its two dead HirError twins are deleted with exactly the 3 direct-caller tests + make_module removed and 7 end-to-end tests kept. I independently reproduced build/clippy/full-suite (1339/0/135), operand-resolved the OpTypeArray length to 32/64 at the two WG candidates, confirmed fail-closed on every reachable path (lower UndefinedStrategyHole on textual F2-strip; codegen UnresolvedSharedLenHole on the enumerator variant), confirmed shared_memory_bytes metadata is computed strictly AFTER the emit backstop (no placeholder-1 leakage), and confirmed the new shared-len hole-ref check is exact parity with the existing @workgroup check (no cross-kernel-sharing regression). No critical bugs, no UB, no races, no vendor divergence. Three non-blocking findings: PW-1 (LOW) a hole used only in a shared-len position is spuriously flagged UnusedStrategyHole because reference-tracking scans annotations only — cosmetic, does not affect discovery/enumeration/codegen; PW-2 (LOW) AT-2984·A's length assertion is a loose OpConstant scan rather than an OpTypeArray-length-operand check; PW-3 (informational) the spec's F2-strip justification is imprecise (the real defense is stronger). PW-1 routes to the Architect as a minor follow-up/defer; none block merge.
